# The status checks required to merge into `develop`, as of 2026-08-07.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#
# A required status context is a string. GitHub matches it against the *name* a
# check run reports, and nothing connects the two. Two things can go wrong and
# neither announces itself:
#
#   * a context names a job that no longer exists -> every PR waits forever on
#     a check that will never report, and the only symptom is "Expected" next
#     to a name nobody recognises;
#   * a job is renamed out from under its context -> the job still runs, still
#     goes green, and stops gating anything at all. Silent. This is the shape
#     of six of the seven inert checks found on 2026-08-06/07.
#
# `scripts/check-workflow-guards.py` reads this file and fails the `Lint` job
# if any context here does not resolve to a job that actually exists across
# `.github/workflows/`, matrix jobs expanded.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO, STATED PLAINLY
#
# It does not verify itself against GitHub. Reading branch protection needs an
# admin token, and the `GITHUB_TOKEN` available to a workflow is not one -- so
# this list can drift from the live setting and `Lint` would not notice. What
# it buys is that the intended set is *in git*, reviewable in a diff, and that
# the far more common failure (a context pointing at a job that is gone) is
# caught. Do not read a green `Lint` as proof this matches the API.
#
# Re-derive the live list, with an admin token:
#
#   gh api repos/cleat-team/cleat/branches/develop/protection/required_status_checks \
#     --jq '.contexts[]' | sort
#
# and compare against this file:
#
#   scripts/check-workflow-guards.py --verify-against-api
#
# When you add or remove a required check, change it in both places in the same
# PR. The API is the one that actually gates; this file is the one that is
# reviewable.
#
# Contexts are job *display names* (`name:`), not job ids, and not workflow
# names. Blank lines and #-comments are ignored.

# NOT required, and deliberately recorded here so the absence is a decision
# rather than an oversight:
#
#   Test Go (crash) on 1.26   -- the twelfth arm of the test-go matrix. The
#                                crash suite is a tier-1 package, so `Tier 1
#                                Gate` (required) already runs it; the per-
#                                package job would only change which name the
#                                failure carries. Same reasoning that applied
#                                to `Test MySQL`/`Test SQL Server` before they
#                                were made required on 2026-08-07.
#   Coverage                  -- the only job in the repo with job-level
#                                `continue-on-error: true`, which is exactly
#                                why it must not be required. Guard 2 below
#                                enforces that pairing in both directions.
#   Lint (advisory)           -- ShellCheck only, as of 2026-08-08. Ruff and
#                                ShellCheck both ran inside the required
#                                `Lint` job under `continue-on-error: true`,
#                                so neither could fail a build; they were
#                                moved here rather than waived in place
#                                (invisible) or made blocking (267 findings
#                                blocking every PR). This job waives nothing
#                                -- it goes red -- it just does not gate.
#                                Ruff has since been promoted back into the
#                                required `Lint` job: its rule set is named
#                                explicitly in python-sdk/pyproject.toml and
#                                its backlog is zero. ShellCheck's 7 findings
#                                are still open and still here. When they
#                                reach zero, promote it and DELETE this job
#                                rather than leaving an empty green one --
#                                then delete this entry too.
#   Test Python 3.10/3.11/3.12
#   Benchmarks, Docs, Examples, and the release/soak/stale/ecosystem jobs.
